channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Samarkand hosts World Conference of Young Parliamentarians on human rights and justice
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians is underway in Samarkand, focusing on ensuring human rights, dignity, and justice amid instability. Around 250 young parliamentarians from nearly 60 countries and representatives from 11 international organizations are participating. The event aims to enhance youth participation in public life and parliamentary activities.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan enhance cooperation in digitalizing plant world data
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are expanding cooperation in digitalizing plant world information. Scientists met to discuss digitizing herbarium collections and preparing data for digital publication. This collaboration aims to integrate national data into international platforms, facilitating research on plant species distribution and biodiversity monitoring.

item.title: Uzbekistan hosts parliamentary forum in Samarkand amid global instability
item.description: Uzbekistan welcomed young parliamentarians to the XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians of the Inter-Parliamentary Union in Samarkand. The event, held for the first time in the country, is seen as a recognition of democratic reforms. Discussions focused on ensuring rights, human dignity, and justice amidst global challenges like climate change and conflict.

item.title: Azerbaijan-Kyrgyzstan Development Fund Capital Increased to $200 Million
item.description: The capital of the Azerbaijan-Kyrgyzstan Development Fund (AKDF) has been increased to $200 million. This decision was formalized through a supplementary agreement signed by the head of the Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers and Azerbaijani officials during the Azerbaijani president's state visit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Unified Energy Audit Procedure for Organizations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has introduced a draft resolution to establish a unified procedure for energy audits of organizations and enterprises. The goal is to create a comprehensive mechanism under the 'On Energy Saving' law, addressing the current lack of a single regulatory act. The proposal outlines mandatory audit cases, periodicity, and requirements for reports and energy-saving plans.

item.title: Tajikistan Allocates 86,000 Hectares for Seedling Cultivation, Plans 2 Billion Trees by 2040
item.description: Tajikistan has designated 86,000 hectares of land for seedling cultivation, with a national plan to plant 2 billion trees by the year 2040. This initiative aims to significantly expand afforestation efforts across the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport faces shortage of qualified personnel
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Transport and Communications is seeking closer cooperation with universities to train specialists needed in the transport sector. The ministry noted a growing demand for engineers and technical staff due to infrastructure development and increased safety requirements.

item.title: New Public Council begins work at Kyrgyzstan’s Ombudsman Institute
item.description: A new Public Council has been established under Kyrgyzstan’s Ombudsman Institute to provide independent advisory support. The council includes experts in human rights and freedoms. Its work will focus on implementing UN recommendations, protecting personal data, and safeguarding environmental rights, according to the ombudsperson.

item.title: Tajikistan's National Bank and UNICEF to expand cooperation on youth financial literacy
item.description: Tajikistan's National Bank and UNICEF plan to expand cooperation in developing financial skills for adolescents and youth, including those with disabilities. Discussions focused on implementing a national financial literacy program and enhancing entrepreneurial opportunities for young people. Both entities aim to boost financial inclusion.

item.title: Brazilian guest praises accessibility of World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan for people with disabilities
item.description: Juliana, a wheelchair user from Brazil attending the 6th World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan, has praised the event's accessibility. She highlighted the organized assistance, special transport, and helpful staff that allowed her to easily attend competitions and visit venues.

item.title: South Korea prepares to deploy troops to Strait of Hormuz to ensure shipping safety
item.description: South Korea is considering deploying military units and special equipment to the Strait of Hormuz by the end of 2026 to ensure the safety of maritime traffic in the strategic waterway. Sources confirm preparatory work is underway, though a final decision has not been made.

item.title: UN warns humanity approaching dangerous global warming limit
item.description: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) warns that humanity can still avoid climate catastrophe but requires immediate action. A new UNEP report highlights record heatwaves and floods as evidence of rising global temperatures, nearing unsafe limits. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius is crucial for humanity's future.

item.title: Tajikistan discusses new climate commitments program NDC 3.0 in Dushanbe
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a roundtable to present and discuss Tajikistan's draft National Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) program. The initiative aims to translate climate commitments into concrete actions in key sectors like energy, water, agriculture, transport, and infrastructure. It also focuses on enhancing the country's resilience to climate risks such as melting glaciers, floods, and droughts.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees decline in gas and oil extraction, rise in electricity and gasoline production
item.description: Uzbekistan's natural gas, oil, and gas condensate extraction decreased in January-July compared to last year. However, gas production significantly recovered in July after a sharp drop in June. Electricity generation increased by 6.4% year-on-year, reaching 52.5 billion kWh. Gasoline production also saw an increase.

item.title: CSTO Joint Military Exercises Planned for 2026
item.description: The Joint Staff of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) announced plans for joint exercises in 2026. The exercises will involve management bodies and forces from CSTO member states including Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan. Key events include a command-staff exercise with the Collective Operational Reaction Forces and joint exercises with the Central Asian Collective Rapid Deployment Forces.

item.title: New 481.5-meter Bridge Over Norin River Completed in Namangan Region
item.description: A new bridge spanning 481.5 meters over the Norin River in Uzbekistan's Namangan region has been completed. The 62 billion soum project connects Uychi, Uchqo'rg'on, and Norin districts to the regional center. This structure is one of the largest and longest built over a river in Uzbekistan since independence. An additional 17.5 kilometers of new road will also be constructed.

item.title: Teenager Who Skipped School for Two Years Sent to Boarding School in Dushanbe
item.description: Police in Dushanbe's Shokhmanzur district apprehended a minor, F. A., for vagrancy. Investigations revealed the teenager had not attended school for two years and was living on the streets. Consequently, court ordered the minor to be removed from parental care and placed in a boarding school for orphans and children without parental care.

item.title: Car Accident in Dangara District Results in Pedestrian Fatality
item.description: A fatal road accident occurred on September 2, 2026, in the Dangara district, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Tajikistan. A Shacman truck struck and killed a pedestrian, Ashurov Mahmadsaid Saidkulovich, while traveling from Bokhtar to Kulyab.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 71.9 Billion Soums of Gas and Electricity Stolen in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzenergoinspeksiya" identified 321 cases of illegal energy resource use in August, resulting in the theft of 71.9 billion Uzbek soums worth of gas and electricity. Investigations into these incidents are ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Liability Insurance for Tour Operators
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved new rules requiring tour operators to provide tourists with medical or accident insurance. Liability limits will vary based on route difficulty, with costs estimated at 400-500 soms per tourist per day. The government expects this to increase tour package costs by only 1-2 percent.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Social Workers Assist Over 40 People with Disabilities at World Nomad Games
item.description: Approximately 100 social workers from Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor are assisting over 40 people with disabilities at the VI World Nomad Games. Special transport is provided for wheelchair users, facilitating their access to events. Both Kyrgyz citizens and foreign visitors have expressed gratitude for the support and inclusive environment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Selling Official Cars Directly to Civil Servants
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a proposal to allow government agencies to sell official vehicles directly to their employees before an auction. The car would be offered to the employee first in line for purchase at market value. If declined, it would proceed to an electronic auction.

item.title: Tajikistan aims to achieve 'A' status for its Ombudsman
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Human Rights Ombudsman met with a UN regional advisor to discuss the institution's development and cooperation in human rights. The Ombudsman's office, currently holding 'B' status since 2012, aims to achieve 'A' status, signifying full compliance with international standards.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan approves concept for science development until 2040
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a concept for the development of science until 2040. This document outlines long-term directions for state policy in science, aiming to foster research, higher education, intellectual property, and innovation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to revise approach to international organization participation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers approved a new procedure for government agencies' cooperation with international organizations. Specific bodies will be assigned to manage relations, coordinate positions, and represent the country, improving cooperation effectiveness and responsibility distribution.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan mandates tour operators to insure tourists
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved rules requiring tour operators to provide mandatory insurance for tourists. This covers medical or accident insurance, with liability limits varying based on the complexity of the tour, ranging from 3 million to 5 million som.

item.title: Tajikistan plans to develop GBAO energy system using digital technologies
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Minister of Energy and Water Resources, Parviz Yakhyezoda, met with AO Pomir Energy in the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) to discuss digitalization. The meeting focused on enhancing the energy sector's digital systems and applying modern technologies. The Sebzor small hydropower plant was also visited.

item.title: Netanyahu: Iranian Regime Will Soon Collapse Amid US Strikes
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated the Iranian regime is struggling to survive following US attacks. He asserted Tehran strikes neighboring countries out of fear of Israel's power, rather than attacking Israel directly.

item.title: Electric Train Service Launched Between Urgench Airport and Khiva
item.description: An electric train service has been launched between Urgench Airport and Khiva in the Khorezm region. The new CR200J train, manufactured by China's CRRC Dalian, can carry 415 passengers at speeds up to 160 km/h.

item.title: American Climber Dies After Falling While Ascending Tajikistan's Peak Ismoil Somoni
item.description: Matt Dawson, a 47-year-old American climber, died after falling approximately 70-80 meters at an altitude of 5800 meters while attempting to summit Peak Ismoil Somoni in Tajikistan. The incident occurred on August 15.

item.title: Three Suspects Arrested for Drug Trafficking in Fergana and Namangan
item.description: Three individuals were apprehended in Fergana and Namangan regions for selling narcotics. Authorities discovered hashish and potent prescription drugs in their possession. Criminal cases have been initiated, and investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presented at CIGRE 2026; NURA Group Supports Global Energy Engagement
item.description: Uzbekistan was presented at CIGRE 2026, with NURA Group endorsing the country's participation in the global energy community. This presentation signifies Uzbekistan's growing role and engagement in international energy discussions and initiatives.

item.title: US Vice President: China Ready to Help Isolate Iran, Cooperate on Economic Pressure
item.description: US Vice President Jey Di Vens stated that China is prepared to assist in isolating Iran and has agreed to cooperate with Washington's plans for economic pressure. He also noted that oil shipments have returned to normal as Tehran lost control in Hormuz.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan allocates 200 million soms for groundwater control and flood prevention
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing a project to manage drainage systems to reduce groundwater levels and prevent flooding and soil salinization. The Ministry of Emergency Situations will oversee operations. 200 million soms have already been allocated from the Stabilization Fund for these works, which include construction and repair of drainage systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans unified state registry for glaciers and enhanced protection measures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing amendments to its law on hydrometeorological activities to establish a unified state registry of glacier data and improve monitoring. The initiative aims to create a systematic state policy for protecting glaciers from pollution and reduction, including research and measures to slow degradation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan could attract 20-30 million tourists annually, says tourism agency head
item.description: Following major events like the World Nomad Games and SCO summits, Kyrgyzstan's tourism interest has surged globally. Eduard Kubatov, head of the State Tourism Agency, predicts tourist numbers could reach 20-30 million annually within years. He urges citizens to prepare accommodations, including yurts, to host visitors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches New Projects Ahead of Independence Day
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched 72 industrial and service projects and 91 social sphere facilities, totaling nearly 50 trillion Uzbekistani soums. These initiatives are expected to create 15,000 jobs and generate an additional 1 trillion soums in annual budget revenue. The economy has grown 2.5 times in the past decade, attracting $160 billion in foreign investment and launching 2,163 major industrial projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ready to Strengthen Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with China
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that relations with China are at an unprecedentedly high level. Astana is prepared to consistently strengthen the eternal comprehensive strategic partnership with Beijing, enriching it with new content and opening new horizons for cooperation. He emphasized that the strong bilateral ties serve the fundamental interests of both nations and contribute to regional peace and stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends Belgrade Summit on Non-Aligned Movement's 65th Anniversary
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Sodik Safoev, participated in a high-level meeting in Belgrade commemorating the 65th anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement. Safoev discussed the movement's current significance and Uzbekistan's preparation to chair it from 2027-2030, highlighting priorities like peace, security, economy, climate change, and youth issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Exports to Hong Kong Surge 22-Fold to $716 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports to Hong Kong reached nearly $716 million in January-July, a 22-fold increase from $32.5 million in the same period last year, according to the National Statistics Committee. This surge has positioned Hong Kong as Uzbekistan's sixth-largest export market, surpassing Turkey and Kyrgyzstan.
